primitives.name: Stochastic Intervention Effect
primitives.verbatim_quote: # [0272] Causal mediation analysis for stochastic interventions (arXiv:1901.02776) **Citation:** Iván Díaz, Nima S.
primitives.assumptions: Piecewise smooth invertibility of the modified treatment policy (A1), common support (A2), and conditional exchangeability (A3).
primitives.breakdown_regime: Violations of A3 (exposure-affected mediator-outcome confounders) lead to biased substitution estimates.

layer2.mapping: Maps the stochastic-intervention direct effect to a conformal prediction interval for the outcome difference under intervention.
layer2.telemetry: Cross-fitted empirical likelihood ratios serve as verification metrics.

primitives.name: Path-Specific Indirect Effect Estimator
primitives.verbatim_quote: # [0272] Causal mediation analysis for stochastic interventions (arXiv:1901.02776) **Citation:** Iván Díaz, Nima S.
primitives.assumptions: Conditional exchangeability (A3) and correct specification of nuisance models for exposure, mediator, and outcome.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Misspecification of the mediator-outcome relationship causes compositional bias in the indirect effect.

layer2.mapping: Replicates the path-specific indirect effect as a posterior predictive distribution under the intervened mediator distribution.
layer2.telemetry: Cross-validation error on the mediator-outcome regression quantifies uncertainty.

primitives.name: Efficient One-Step Estimator
primitives.verbatim_quote: # [0272] Causal mediation analysis for stochastic interventions (arXiv:1901.02776) **Citation:** Iván Díaz, Nima S.
primitives.assumptions: Doubly robust nuisance models and sample splitting to control variance inflation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Overfitting of nuisance models leads to inefficient influence functions and inflated standard errors.

layer2.mapping: Derives a semiparametric efficiency bound kernel that optimally weights the score equations for the direct effect.
layer2.telemetry: Empirical sandwich variance estimates provide robust standard errors.

primitives.name: Cross-Fitting
primitives.verbatim_quote: # [0272] Causal mediation analysis for stochastic interventions (arXiv:1901.02776) **Citation:** Iván Díaz, Nima S.
primitives.assumptions: Independence within folds and sufficient overlap across folds.
primitives.breakdown_regime: High correlation between training and validation sets biases the cross-fit estimate toward the training set distribution.

layer2.mapping: Maps cross-fitting to a leave-one-out Bayesian updating scheme, where each fold provides an independent posterior update.
layer2.telemetry: Variance across fold predictions serves as a diagnostic for model stability.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core contribution is a unified substitution estimator that bridges the gap between experimental identification and observational mediation analysis. It leverages the efficient influence function to achieve double robustness and local efficiency, while the cross-fitting procedure mitigates overfitting. However, the method relies on the untestable assumption A3, which can introduce bias if exposure affects mediator-outcome confounders. The approach is computationally intensive due to ensemble learning of nuisance models, and its performance depends critically on the quality of the Super Learner ensembles.
